question.text: Which of the following has longest <math> <mrow> <mtext>C</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>O</mtext></mrow> </math> bond length? (Free <math> <mrow> <mtext>C</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>O</mtext></mrow> </math> bond length in <math> <mrow> <mtext>CO</mtext></mrow> </math> is <math> <mrow> <mtext>1</mtext><mtext>.128 </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mover> <mtext>A</mtext> <mtext>o</mtext> </mover> </mrow> </math>).

options.text: <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><msub><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math>

solution.text:
Metal carbon bond in metal carbonyls possess both σ and π character. M−C π bond is formed by donation of a pair of electrons from filled orbital of metal into vacant antibonding π orbital of CO . CO bond length increases if M has more tendency to donate lone pair.

Tendency to donate lone pair is Fe 2− > Co − >Ni> Mn +
